headline: Southborough boards set positions on Special Town Meeting warrant articles, narrowed Neary School building plans, and opened reviews for a proposed Costco.
synopsis: Ahead of the October Special Town Meeting, town boards took conflicting stances on key warrant articles, including Community Preservation Act appropriations for golf course irrigation and a pedestrian trail bridge, as well as a proposed two-family zoning amendment. The Elementary School Building Committee narrowed its design alternatives for Neary Elementary School, eliminating an exterior addition in favor of interior renovation options and a baseline study. The Planning Board opened its public hearing on Costco Wholesale's proposal to construct a 167,000-square-foot warehouse and 30-position gas station on the Westborough border. Meanwhile, municipal departments began modeling FY28 operating budgets under both level-service assumptions and zero-growth cut scenarios tied to a potential tax override vote. In governance moves, the Select Board appointed Amy Berry as interim town clerk while the town prepares to vote on making the position permanently appointed.

top_items.title: Neary School Building Options Narrowed to Three
top_items.why: The Elementary School Building Committee voted to eliminate an exterior addition and focus future architectural studies on interior renovations and a $15 million baseline.
top_items.body: After reviewing cost estimates ranging from $24.4 million to $49.2 million, including a projected $4.5 million roof replacement, the Elementary School Building Committee voted 3-1 to eliminate Option 4 due to high site costs and poor soil conditions. The committee voted 4-0 to direct consultants to focus on Option 1 (code-compliance renovation), Option 3 (enclosing the courtyard to build a full-size gymnasium), and an analysis of a $15 million baseline scope. Educators strongly supported Option 3 for meeting programming needs without encroaching on outdoor athletic fields.

top_items.title: Costco Wholesale Presents Route 9 Warehouse and Gas Station
top_items.why: Costco presented initial site, grading, and traffic plans for a 167,000-square-foot retail warehouse and 30-pump gas station on Coslin Drive.
top_items.body: Costco Wholesale and its project team submitted applications for site plan review and special permits on a 26.12-acre parcel on the Southborough and Westborough town line. The initial hearing drew resident concerns regarding severe congestion on Route 9, cut-through traffic along Flagg Road, truck turnaround constraints at Route 85, and environmental buffers. The Planning Board voted 4-0 to continue the hearing to October 19, 2026, while peer reviews proceed.

top_items.title: Town Boards Split Over CPA Golf Course Irrigation Funding
top_items.why: The Advisory Committee voted 0-7 against recommending $433,546 in CPA funds for golf course irrigation, while the Select Board and CPC supported the article.
top_items.body: Town officials finalized Special Town Meeting Article 3 seeking supplemental Community Preservation Act funds after project costs rose to $1,087,296 following initial bids. The plan allocates $100,000 from the Golf Course Revolving Fund and $433,546 in CPA funds to replace the failing irrigation system. The Select Board voted 5-0 and the Community Preservation Committee voted 4-1 to recommend approval, but the Advisory Committee voted 0-7 against it, arguing the municipal course should fund capital repairs through golfer user fees rather than tax revenues.

top_items.title: Peninsula Trail Footbridge Funding Meets Strong Opposition
top_items.why: The Select Board and Advisory Committee both voted against recommending $217,318 in CPA funds for a pedestrian bridge connecting sections of the Peninsula Trail.
top_items.body: The Trails Committee sought $217,318 in additional CPA funding for a 65-foot prefabricated pedestrian footbridge on the Framingham line after previous bids surpassed the original $211,232 appropriation, bringing total estimated costs to $428,550. While the Community Preservation Committee voted unanimously to support the article, the Select Board voted 1-4 against it and the Advisory Committee voted 0-7 against it, citing high project costs during a difficult fiscal cycle. The Trails Committee agreed to prepare outreach and evaluate extending existing funds to 2029.

top_items.title: Two-Family Zoning Amendment Generates Divided Recommendations
top_items.why: The Select Board and ZBA endorsed an article allowing two-family dwellings by removing a two-year waiting period, but the Advisory Committee voted 3-4 against recommending it.
top_items.body: Special Town Meeting Article 2 proposes updating town zoning bylaws to define two-family dwellings and remove the mandatory two-year waiting period required to convert single-family homes into two-family units. Proponents emphasized creating regional housing variety, while opponents raised concerns regarding neighborhood density, school enrollment impacts, and septic capacity. The Select Board voted 4-1 (and later 5-0 on revised text) in favor, the ZBA endorsed the changes 5-0, but the Advisory Committee voted 3-4 against recommending approval. The Planning Board continued its public hearing to October 17.

top_items.title: Departments Prepare Severe Cut Scenarios for FY28 Operating Budget
top_items.why: Town administration instructed departments to model FY28 budgets with zero-percent increases in preparation for a possible spring tax override vote.
top_items.body: Town departments began drafting two FY28 budget submissions: Request A maintaining level services, and Request B modeling a zero-percent increase if an operational override fails. The Library Board of Trustees evaluated Request B cuts that would eliminate programming and professional development while halving subscription databases, while the Board of Health and Conservation Commission faced cutting staff hours. Simultaneously, the Personnel Board voted 4-0 to recommend a 5 percent total wage adjustment for FY28, consisting of a 3 percent cost-of-living adjustment and a 2 percent step increment.

top_items.title: Interim Town Clerk Appointed Ahead of Governance Ballot Vote
top_items.why: The Select Board appointed Amy Berry as interim town clerk through May 2027 as Southborough prepares to vote on converting the post to an appointed position.
top_items.body: Following the retirement of long-time Town Clerk Jim Hegarty, the Select Board voted 5-0 to appoint former deputy clerk Amy Berry as interim town clerk from October 1, 2026, through May 11, 2027. Special Town Meeting Article 1 proposes changing the position from elected to appointed, which was endorsed 5-0 by the Select Board and 6-0 by the Advisory Committee. If approved at Town Meeting, the change will go before Southborough voters at the May 2027 annual town election.
